public.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
public.description: Process a fresh timestamped key-value store. ["set",key,value,timestamp] stores a string and returns null. ["get",key,timestamp] returns the value at the greatest stored timestamp no larger than the requested one, or "" when absent. Set timestamps increase strictly for each key; get timestamps may be arbitrary. Keys and values contain 1 to 20 lowercase letters or digits, timestamps are 1 to 1000000000, and there are 0 to 500 operations. Across all operations, key and value strings contain at most 10000 characters in total. Return one result per operation; there is no constructor operation.
hints: Maintain a sorted timestamp history for each key.
Binary search for the first entry later than the query.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026, for a standard algorithmic problem. No third-party exercise text or solution code used.

explanation: Per-key append-only histories remain sorted. Upper-bound search locates the final timestamp at or before the query. O(1) set, O(log history length) get, O(number of sets) storage.
